key.description: A data key: lowercase letters, digits, _, - and dots, up to 64 characters. A Home Assistant entity id is a valid key.

name.description: A box or display name: lowercase letters, digits, _ and -, up to 32 characters.

notify_key.description: A notification key: letters, digits, _ and -, up to 48 characters. It is the topic's last segment.

colors.description: Colours as #RRGGBB, like a team's or a platform's.

time.description: An RFC 3339 time with an offset, like 2026-10-01T07:05:00-04:00.

tier.description: How loud a notification is: where it shows, for how long, and what it sounds like.

screen.description: A screen's name, as the layout lists it.

font.description: The face for a card's number (or a text card's title and big value, or the clock): pixel is the 5 × 7 face, flip split-flap tiles, nixie glowing tubes (digits; anything else an unlit tube), segment a 7-segment display (digits and the letters it can make; anything else an unlit digit), space a heavy rounded face, retro64 an 8 × 8 face in the style of '80s home computers, alagard a medieval blackletter face, celtic rounded brush-stroke capitals, comicoro a slanted comic hand (each by its own designer; credits on the Fonts page).

oneOf.description: A PixelBar icon by name, or a Material Design icon as mdi:name, drawn as the nearest PixelBar icon.
A custom icon: up to 20 × 20, up to 16 colours, 4 bits per pixel, row-major, base64.

palette.description: Up to 16 colours; each pixel is an index into this list.

data.description: The pixels, 4 bits each, row by row, base64.

icon.description: An icon: a PixelBar icon by name, a Material Design icon as mdi:name, or a custom one drawn inline.

oneOf.description: A built-in pattern (beep, double, triple, chime, westminster, rising, falling, done, alert, alarm, siren, beepboop, garage, none) or the id of a sound sent on pixelbar/all/asset/sound/<id>.
A pattern with a repeat, or a tune of your own.

repeat.description: How many times to play it, 1 to 10.

rtttl.description: A Nokia RTTTL tune, name:d=4,o=6,b=120:notes. Cut off at 128 notes.

steps.description: frequency:milliseconds pairs, 0 Hz for a rest.

sound.description: What the buzzer plays: a built-in pattern or saved tune by name, or { rtttl }, { steps } or { pattern, repeat }.

image_ref.description: A picture by id, or the picture itself (stored under its id for later).

data.description: The pixels as rgb565, row by row, base64.

big.description: A large number, beside the title on the right (like 5 MIN) or across the top. Hidden on the right when the box is too narrow.

value.description: The number. Digits and a colon; tokens like {elapsed_min} work.

font.description: The number's font: flip and nixie draw the digits their own way.

at.description: right: beside the title, the usual. top: across the card, with the title and the small print under it as far as they fit; a value too wide scrolls.

progress.description: A bar. With playing true and an updated time, the display moves it on its own between updates.

value.description: How far along, in the same unit as max.

max.description: The full length, like a song's duration in seconds.

playing.description: While true, the display moves the bar on its own from updated.

rule.description: Holds while a value passes the test: above or below a number, equals a value, or not a value. With no test it holds while the value is on, true, playing, home or a number above 0. data names a data key; entity names a Home Assistant entity, which the integration sends under its entity id.

above.description: Holds while the value is above this number.

below.description: Holds while the value is below this number.

equals.description: Holds while the value is exactly this, like "playing" or 0.

not.description: Holds while the value is anything but this.

anyOf.description: Holds while every rule in it holds.

all.description: Up to 8 rules or time windows; the group holds while every one does.

clock_rule.description: Holds during a time of day, on some days of the week, in the display's local time.

after.description: From this time (HH:MM). Midnight by default.

before.description: Until this time (HH:MM), not including it. If it's earlier than after, the window runs past midnight. Midnight by default.

days.description: Only on these days. Every day by default.

time.description: A time window: after, before and days.

at.description: Where it goes: around (an outline), below (a shadow), above, left or right. around by default.

outline.description: An outline round the words and numbers, so they read over a busy background: a colour as #RRGGBB (all round), { color, at } to put it on one side, like a shadow below, or none.

effects.description: How the words sit in the weather sky: behind (the weather stays behind them) or around (the words are in it: near rain falls in front and splashes on the letters, snow settles on them).

case.description: How words show: upper, in capitals (the usual LED look), or as_written, keeping lowercase and accents as you typed them, like Adaléa. A font without lowercase (the small one) shows capitals either way.
